_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 2 Mathematics unit lecture film, Patterns That Grow. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. Every beat is one narration clip; art.at names the phrases a picture waits for, and the page refuses to load if a phrase is not in its beat's say. The chapters follow the lesson page's own steps in order - the part that repeats (step 4), what comes next and mending a gap (steps 5 and 6), counting on in steps (step 8), how a number pattern goes up and the missing number (steps 9 and 10), counting back (step 11) and the hundred square (step 12) - in the lesson's own shapes (orange circle, teal square) and the lesson's own numbers (3, 5, 7, 9, 11; 20, 25, 30, 35; 15, 20, 25, 30; 10, 20, gap, 40; 50, 40, 30, 20; 5, 15, 25, 35).
title: Patterns That Grow
subtitle: Grade 2 Mathematics
objectives: Use familiar language associated with patterns and randomness, including regular pattern and random pattern.
Count on and count back in ones, twos, fives or tens, starting from any number (from 0 to 100).
Recognise, describe and extend numerical sequences (from 0 to 100).

beats.say: Some patterns repeat, over and over. Other patterns grow.
Find the part that repeats, or find the step. Then you know what comes next.
Here is a line of shapes. Circle, square, circle, square.
One small part comes round again and again. Can you see it?
Here it is. The part that repeats is circle, square.
It is two shapes long. Say it six times and you have the whole line.
Now a longer part: circle, square, square. Three shapes, whole every time.
Once you have found the part, you can say what comes next.
Circle, square, square, circle. What shape comes after that?
Square. The part tells you, not the shape just before it.
If a shape falls out of the middle, the part mends it.
Numbers make patterns too. You count on in steps.
Start at 3 and count on in twos. 3, 5, 7, 9, 11.
Every jump is the same size. You add 2 each time.
You can start anywhere. 20, 25, 30, 35 goes up in fives.

scenes.heading: How much does it go up?

beats.say: Now a number pattern. 15, 20, 25, 30. How does it go up?
Look at the jumps between them, not just at the numbers.
15 to 20 is 5. And 20 to 25 is 5 again.
Always check two jumps. One jump on its own can trick you.
Every jump here is 5, so the pattern goes up in fives.
Now one number is hiding. 10, 20, gap, 40.
It goes up in tens, so the gap must be 30.
Counting back takes the same step away each time.
Start at 50 and count back in tens. 50, 40, 30, 20.
The numbers get smaller. If one gets bigger, you went the wrong way.
Number patterns hide in the hundred square as well.
These coloured numbers are 5, 15, 25 and 35.
They go straight down one column. Each one is ten more.
So the next one is 45. Down one row always adds ten.
A repeating pattern has a part that comes round again.

at.part: a part that comes round again

beats.say: A number pattern goes up, or back, by the same step.
You can count on in twos, fives or tens, from any number.
Find the step, and you can always say what comes next.
